jobs.title: Operations Lead (Member Support)
jobs.description:
About the role

The Support team is the heart of Thatch – the people who help members navigate their benefits when it matters, assist employers in administering benefits, and partner with brokers to serve their books of business. Support is where our mission to build a healthcare system people love is delivered, one interaction at a time.

As Support Lead, you'll own daily execution of our support function across members, employers, and brokers, and the long game of scaling it. You'll coach and develop a team of specialists, stand up new support channels, and prepare the team for Open Enrollment, our highest-stakes period of the year. You'll be the operational and cultural backbone of the team: managing escalations, jumping into the queue when it counts, partnering across the company to fix the upstream issues that drive support volume, and building an uplifting team culture.

This is a role for leaders who find genuine satisfaction in frontline support, coaching people into their next chapter, and the gritty, behind-the-scenes work required to deliver a best-in-class support experience at scale.

What you'll do

- Own daily execution of the support queue – oversee day-to-day operation of the support queue across channels, meeting SLAs and delivering best-in-class support to members, employers, and brokers as we scale. Adapt quickly when volume spikes, incidents emerge, or new issue patterns surface.

- Scale the support function – stand up new support models like phone support, train and uplevel specialists into functional experts, and drive efficiency through AI, automation, tooling, and cross-functional partnership so the team can absorb growth without scaling headcount linearly. Own planning and execution of seasonal staffing to handle OEP volume.

- Coach and develop your team – run 1:1s, invest in specialists' careers, grow the next generation of support leaders at Thatch, and deliver direct, timely feedback on quality and performance.

- Drive cross-functional impact on the customer experience – partner with teams across Thatch to highlight and tackle customer and support team pain points, and surface opportunities to build a better product experience that reduces inbound support volume and addresses operational inefficiencies and gaps.

- Cultivate a culture that drives the team and company forward – build a supportive, collaborative environment, recognize hard work and difficult moments, and make the team's contributions visible across the company.

- Own escalations end-to-end – serve as the escalation point for customer issues and incidents, see problems through to resolution, and convert insights from escalations into product, process, and tooling improvements that prevent recurrence.

- Stay connected to customer needs and the frontline – own escalations and jump into team queues to get things done. Take on difficult cases and operational work that keeps you well-versed on the customer experience and state of support, and helps you see where the next investment in product, process, and tooling should land.

Background we're looking for

- Minimum 7 years of relevant experience, including 3+ years as a people manager.

- Minimum 3 years of experience in a customer-facing support role supporting a complex benefits, healthcare, or finance product.

- Experience managing high-volume, seasonal support queues across live channels (phone, email, chat).

- Unshakeable empathy and dedication to solving the hairiest customer problems.

- Proven ability to deliver tailored coaching that closes performance gaps and grows specialists into future leaders. You know how to bring out the best in the people around you and foster a culture of accountability.

- Extreme detail-orientedness. No minor change, inconsistency, or error gets past you.

- Comfort leading teams through fast-paced change (new tools, new processes, new ways of working) with a relentlessly optimistic mindset.

- Track record of turning frontline insight into product and process change — you've partnered closely with product and engineering teams to fix the upstream issues that drive support volume.

- Demonstrated passion for Thatch's mission.

Experience we’d be particularly excited about

- Experience leading in a high-growth or startup environment.

- Experience supporting customers within the healthcare industry.

- Experience supporting multiple customer personas (e.g. consumers, businesses, partners/brokers) within a single team or queue.

- Experience using AI, automation, or tooling to scale a support function.

- Experience managing seasonal contractors or BPO vendors providing customer support in regulated industries.

- Low ego. You are unafraid to get your hands dirty and balance taking on support tickets with your daily responsibilities.

What to expect

We interview rigorously based on integrity, talent, and drive; the trust we display in our teammates from day 1 is a reflection of the confidence we have in this process. We aim to evaluate the things you’ll be doing every day as best we can, and we move quickly. Here's what to expect:

- 30 minute video meeting to talk through your background and interest in Thatch

- 45 minute video meeting with the hiring manager to dive deeper into your experience and the role

- 30 minute video meetings to meet 2-3 members of the team

- 30 minute video meeting with our founders to discuss your approach to culture and our operating principles

Estimated Compensation Range
$115,000 — $130,000 USD

About Thatch

We’re a fully distributed early stage company using technology to change the way America does healthcare. We’re a happy, friendly, high-velocity team. You can read  more on Thatch here .

jobs.title: Revenue Strategy & Operations Associate
jobs.description:
About the role

This role sits inside the Revenue Strategy function and reports directly to the Head of Revenue Strategy & Operations. The mandate: turn the signal that already exists in Salesforce, Redshift, and our operational data into analysis that informs how leadership allocates resources and makes commercial decisions — and run the operating cadences that deliver that work reliably.

The role blends two disciplines. The first is analytical execution: building the queries, models, and analytical outputs the Revenue Strategy function runs on. The second is program execution: owning recurring deliverables end-to-end — managing inputs, timelines, and stakeholders so that leadership's operating rhythm runs without being chased. You'll partner closely with the Head of Revenue Strategy & Operations, who shapes the strategic recommendations, board narratives, and territory and comp decisions your work feeds — but you own your workstreams from question to delivered answer.

What you'll do

- Channel and pipeline analytics. Thatch sells through multiple GTM motions simultaneously, each with different unit economics and conversion dynamics. You will build and maintain the recurring analyses that make those differences visible — win rates by segment, geography, and channel; broker quoting and attribution analysis; and pipeline pacing against target.

- Forecasting and pipeline quality support. You will maintain the analytical layer behind our pipeline quality and forecasting standards — snapshot queries, coverage ratios, and stage conversion analysis — and flag when the data says the forecast is at risk.

- Operating cadence execution . You will run the recurring rhythms of the Revenue Strategy function end-to-end: MBR/QBR data builds, forecast cycle prep, and incentive program tracking (e.g., SPIFs) — sequencing dependencies, gathering inputs from Sales, Finance, and Marketing stakeholders, and delivering on deadline without escalation.

- GTM data infrastructure. You will own the SQL layer that Revenue Strategy runs on: clean, documented, reusable queries against Salesforce and Redshift, and the BI views that keep leadership's standing metrics accurate and current.

- Systems and process rollout support. You will support GTM systems changes from spec through rollout — partnering with RevOps on Salesforce data hygiene, field and flow changes, and validation that downstream reporting survives the change.

- Ad hoc analysis. You will support the Head of Revenue Strategy on board preparation, QBR/MBR builds, segment and territory analysis, and other work that requires turning raw data into a clear finding — fast.

Background we're looking for

- Experience. 2–4 years in GTM analytics, RevOps, BizOps, or a related analytical role in a high-growth technology company. Exposure to sales or revenue teams is strongly preferred.

- Technical fluency. Strong SQL is required. Experience with Salesforce as a data source, Redshift or Snowflake, and a BI tool (Sigma, Metabase, Tableau, or equivalent) is expected. Python or dbt is a plus.

- Analytical rigor. You can structure an analysis, sanity-check your own work, and know when a result is right versus when it merely looks right. Familiarity with core GTM math — win rates, conversion, coverage, unit economics — is expected.

- Communication. The output of this role is not dashboards; it is answers. You can write a clear, concise summary of what an analysis shows and what it implies.

- Ownership. You flag when a number is wrong before someone else notices. You treat the work as yours.

What to expect

We interview rigorously based on integrity, talent, and drive; the trust we display in our teammates from day 1 is a reflection of the confidence we have in this process. We aim to evaluate the things you’ll be doing every day as best we can, and we move quickly. Here's what to expect:

- 30 minute video meeting to talk through your background and interest in Thatch

- 45 minute video meeting with the hiring manager to dive deeper into your experience and the role

- 60 minute video meeting to meet 2 members of the team

- 60 minute video meeting with the hiring manager to work through a live case study

- 45 minute video meeting with department leadership to address career goals and alignment to role

- 45 minute video meeting with our founders to discuss your approach to culture and our operating principles

Estimated Compensation Range
$135,000 — $160,000 USD

About Thatch

We’re a fully distributed early stage company using technology to change the way America does healthcare. We’re a happy, friendly, high-velocity team. You can read  more on Thatch here .

jobs.title: GTM Analytics Lead
jobs.description:
About the role

This role leads GTM Analytics within the Revenue Strategy function and reports directly to the Head of Revenue Strategy & Operations. You will own how Thatch measures GTM performance, understands channel economics, and governs the data foundation behind commercial decisions.

The role covers three areas: GTM performance and channel economics, GTM data strategy and governance, and analytical support for forecasting, planning, and executive reporting. Your work is the analytical engine behind all three.

You set the analytical agenda for your areas. You decide which questions matter most, focus effort on the highest-value work, and turn findings into recommendations that change where Thatch invests. You will partner closely with Marketing, Data Science, Finance, and RevOps.

What you'll do

GTM Performance and Channel Economics

- Build performance frameworks that show GTM health across the full customer lifecycle, from lead through close, onboarding, retention, and expansion.

- Own the framework for comparing Thatch's GTM motions: win rates, CAC, payback, and conversion by segment, geography, and channel, plus broker attribution and quoting performance.

- Partner with Marketing on funnel and attribution, with Data Science on modeling and segmentation, and with Finance on unit economics and scenario analysis.

- Spot emerging trends early and recommend where to invest and where to pull back, including clear tradeoffs.

- Prioritize the analytics roadmap by business impact.

GTM Data Strategy and Governance

- Own the GTM data strategy and set priorities for the integrity, scalability, and evolution of the GTM team’s data foundation, in partnership with Data Science.

- Define and govern core GTM metrics, business logic, and data standards so every standing number is consistent, auditable, and reconciles with Finance.

- Set governance for definitions, lineage, quality, and usage in partnership with RevOps, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance.

- Define GTM business requirements before technical work begins. RevOps and Engineering keep ownership of technical build.

- Prioritize GTM data initiatives and make sequencing recommendations based on dependencies and business impact.

- Make sure data assets support critical use cases, including forecasting, pipeline management, planning, compensation, and performance measurement.

- Drive adoption of governed metrics and BI across GTM teams.

Forecasting, Planning, and Reporting Support

- Build and maintain the analytical inputs behind the forecast: pipeline snapshots, coverage, stage conversion, and pacing.

- Supply the data and models that feed target setting, capacity planning, and compensation analysis.

- Deliver complete, accurate analytics for board, QBR, and MBR materials on every cycle.

- Flag when the data signals risk to the forecast or plan.

Strategic Decision Support

- Break down ambiguous GTM questions, combining data, financial implications, and operational context.

- Lead high-stakes segment, channel, and territory analyses from problem definition through recommendation.

- Present findings, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to senior leadership.

Background we're looking for

- Experience. 5 to 8 years in GTM analytics, RevOps, BizOps, strategy, or FP&A at a high-growth B2B company, with direct partnership with sales, marketing, and finance leadership.

- Technical depth. Expert SQL. Deep experience with sales and product telemetry data, mainstream business intelligence tools.

- Data governance. Experience owning metric definitions and data standards, and turning business requirements into technical specs in a modern data stack.

- Systems thinking. You understand dependencies across CRM, warehouse, BI, and GTM execution, and how a field change flows through to a board metric.

- Commercial judgment. Command of GTM and SaaS metrics, including win rates, conversion, attribution, CAC, payback, and retention.

- Cross-functional influence. You align Marketing, Data Science, Finance, and RevOps on shared definitions and priorities without formal authority.

- Executive communication. You deliver answers, not dashboards, and turn complex analysis into clear recommendations.

- Ownership. You own the numbers, catch errors first, and raise risks early.

Experience we’d be particularly excited about

- Comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, balancing speed and rigor with limited resources and evolving data

What to expect

We interview rigorously based on integrity, talent, and drive; the trust we display in our teammates from day 1 is a reflection of the confidence we have in this process. We aim to evaluate the things you’ll be doing every day as best we can, and we move quickly. Here's what to expect:

jobs.description:
About the role

Thatch Market is growing, and so is the partner ecosystem behind it. We’re looking for a Strategic Partnerships Manager to own the partners already powering the Market and help decide who we bring in next.

You’ll manage and grow our existing partnerships, identify where the Market should expand, and source and close the partners that can get us there. You’ll build deep relationships with our partners and look for opportunities to expand what we can do together, both within the Market and across Thatch.

This is a high-ownership role with the opportunity to shape what Thatch Market becomes as we scale.

What you will do

- Own our partner ecosystem. Manage our portfolio of Market partners, from performance and ongoing relationships to renewals, growth opportunities, and offboarding.

- Figure out what’s next. Understand what our members need, identify gaps in the Market, and determine which partners and categories we should pursue.

- Bring great partners to Thatch. Source, pitch, negotiate, and close strategic healthcare and service partners.

- Build partnerships that make sense. Structure commercial models that work for Thatch and our partners, with a clear understanding of the economics and tradeoffs behind them.

- Make partnerships work in practice. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and other teams to launch new partnerships, solve problems, and make them successful over time.

What we're looking for

- 4+ years of experience in strategic partnerships, business development, or a similar role, ideally in technology.

- A track record of personally sourcing, negotiating, and closing strategic partnerships.

- Experience building and owning strong partner relationships after launch and growing them over time.

- Strong commercial judgment and comfort navigating deal structure, economics, and tradeoffs.

- The ability to see beyond the immediate deal and identify broader opportunities for a partnership.

- Strong cross-functional skills and the ability to move work forward across multiple teams.

Experience that stands out

- Experience in healthcare, benefits, fintech, or another complex industry.

- Experience building partnerships that are closely connected to a product or customer experience.

- Experience working closely with Product and Engineering to turn partner needs into scalable solutions.

- Unshakable optimism in the face of adversity.

How we work

- We give people ownership and trust them to make good decisions.

- We move quickly, learn from customers, and improve continuously.

- We solve hard problems together, regardless of team or title.

- We care more about building the right thing than following a perfect process.

What to expect

We aim to keep the process thoughtful, rigorous, and efficient. Most candidates complete it within three weeks. You can expect:

- An initial conversation with a recruiter.

- A conversation with the hiring manager to dig into your experience and the role.

- Conversations with teammates across business development, product, and engineering.

- A final conversation with executive leadership.

jobs.title: Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
About the role

Thatch is rethinking how health insurance is provided and used in the US, and compliance is core to what we do. Our compliance obligations span insurance regulation, financial services, employee benefits, and IRS requirements–often at the same time. You'll be part of the team that keeps that program running: reviewing marketing and advertising against state insurance rules and federal advertising requirements, executing our monitoring and testing procedures and documenting the results, and working second-line review of customer accounts and transaction monitoring escalations. You'll do this alongside experienced compliance and legal colleagues and, regardless of your level, will learn so much as you help build this function out. We're looking for someone with a few years of compliance or regulatory experience who is precise, organized, and genuinely interested in  why a rule exists, not just whether a box got checked.

What you'll do

- Review marketing copy and customer-facing materials against policy, rules, and requirements. Maintain the advertising files and approval records those rules require

- Support monitoring and testing procedures: pull samples, gather evidence, document results, and track identified issues through remediation

- Work second-line review of customer onboarding (KYB/C) and transaction monitoring escalations, complete enhanced due diligence (EDD) requests, document dispositions, and escalate cases that warrant review by senior team members or financial partners

- Maintain compliance recordkeeping, policy and procedure documentation, and the evidence needed to support audits, examinations, and partner diligence

- Partner with teams around Thatch including Marketing, Product, Operations, and Financial Partnerships to answer routine compliance questions and route the harder ones to the right person

- Support employee compliance training delivery and completion tracking

Background we're looking for

- Bachelor's degree with 3+ years of experience in compliance, regulatory operations, risk, audit, or a closely related function

- Exposure to at least one regulated environment — insurance, banking or payments, securities, healthcare, or benefits

- Strong writing skills and real precision with detail; you can document what you did clearly enough that someone else can rely on it a year later

- Highly organized with a demonstrated ability to manage recurring workflows and competing deadlines without dropping threads

- Curiosity about overlapping regulatory regimes and the judgment to know when to ask rather than assume

- Good sense of humor… you work in compliance, so it's ok if it is a little dark

Experience we’d be particularly excited about

- Experience in health insurance, financial services, or another regulated industry

- Hands-on KYB/C, AML, or transaction monitoring alert review experience

- Experience executing control testing or supporting an audit or regulatory examination

- Comfort with modern compliance tooling and an interest in using AI to make recurring review work faster and better documented

- Experience in a startup or high-growth environment where the procedure didn't exist yet or decision frameworks are evolving

What to expect
